claim: SFTP connectors have two networking options, Service Managed and VPC Lattice; with Service Managed the connectors reach the remote SFTP server over the public internet and you manage no additional networking resources.
question: What networking options are supported by SFTP connectors when creating connections to remote SFTP servers?

evidence.quote: You can choose from two networking options – Service Managed or VPC Lattice. When using Service Managed option, connectors will connect to remote SFTP server over the public internet and you do not need to create or manage any additional networking resources.

claim: With the VPC Lattice option, SFTP connectors route connections to the remote server through your VPC, so they can reach privately hosted servers over existing networks such as AWS Direct Connect or VPN.
question: Can I use SFTP connectors to connect with servers within a private network?

values.display: route SFTP connections to the remote server via your VPC environment

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family SFTP connectors, VPC Lattice egress

evidence.quote: When using the VPC Lattice option, connectors will route SFTP connections to the remote server via your VPC environment, enabling you to connect with privately hosted servers over existing networks like AWS Direct Connect or VPN channels to the remote servers.

claim: When you create an SFTP connector with Egress Type Service Managed, Transfer Family provides static IP addresses for the connector by default, which a business partner can allow-list in its firewall.
question: Can I configure my SFTP connector to present a static IP address to the remote server?

values.display: static IP addressed for with your connectors by default

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family SFTP connectors, Service Managed egress

evidence.quote: Yes. When you create a SFTP connector with Egress Type as Service Managed, Transfer Family will provide static IP addressed for with your connectors by default that can be used to allow-list connections on your business partner’s firewall.

claim: You can schedule SFTP connector file transfers with Amazon EventBridge Scheduler, using the Transfer Family StartFileTransfer or StartDirectoryListing API as the target of the schedule.
question: Can I schedule my file transfers using SFTP connectors?

evidence.quote: Yes. You can schedule file transfers using Amazon EventBridge Scheduler. Create a schedule that meets your business’s needs using EventBridge’s Scheduler and specify AWS Transfer Family’s StartFileTransfer API, or StartDirectoryListing API, as the universal target for your schedule.

claim: Files that Transfer Family stores in an S3 bucket can be encrypted with S3 server-side encryption (SSE-S3) or with AWS KMS (SSE-KMS).
question: What are my options to encrypt data at rest?

values.display: Amazon S3 Server-Side Encryption (SSE-S3) or Amazon KMS (SSE-KMS)

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family, files stored in Amazon S3

evidence.quote: You can choose to encrypt files stored your bucket using Amazon S3 Server-Side Encryption (SSE-S3) or Amazon KMS (SSE-KMS).

claim: You can assign a single IAM role to all your Transfer Family users and use logical directory mappings that set which absolute S3 bucket paths are visible to each user and how the paths are presented to their clients.
question: I have 100s of SFTP/FTPS/FTP users who have similar access settings but to different portions of my bucket. Can I set them up using the same IAM Role and policy?

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family users on Amazon S3

evidence.quote: Yes. You can assign a single IAM Role for all your users and use logical directory mappings that specify which absolute Amazon S3 bucket paths you want to make visible to your end users and how you these paths presented to them by their clients.

claim: Files transferred through Transfer Family are stored as objects in your S3 bucket with a one-to-one mapping between files and objects, which allows native access with AWS services for processing or analytics.
question: How are files stored in my Amazon S3 bucket transferred using AWS Transfer?

values.display: one-to-one mapping between files and objects

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family with Amazon S3

evidence.quote: Files transferred over the supported protocols are stored as objects in your Amazon S3 bucket, and there is a one-to-one mapping between files and objects enabling native access to these objects using AWS services for processing or analytics.

claim: You can attach an FSx File Gateway to shares on up to 5 file systems as long as they are all members of the same Active Directory domain, because the gateway joins only a single AD domain.
question: Can Amazon FSx File Gateway be connected to more than one Amazon FSx for Windows file system?

qualifiers.condition: all file systems in the same Active Directory domain

evidence.quote: Yes. You are allowed to attach a gateway to shares on up to 5 file systems as long as they are all members of the same Active Directory domain. Amazon FSx File Gateway will only join a single Active Directory Domain.

note: Amazon FSx File Gateway is on the AWS maintenance list since 2024-10-28 (see fsx-change-fsx-file-gateway-maintenance-2024-10); teach it as old-question knowledge.

claim: Amazon FSx File Gateway supports up to 50 shares and 500 active client sessions in a single instance configuration.
question: How many sessions and file shares does Amazon FSx File Gateway support?

qualifiers.scope: per Amazon FSx File Gateway instance

evidence.quote: Amazon FSx File Gateway supports up to 50 shares and 500 active client sessions connected to Amazon FSx File Gateway instances in a single instance configuration.

note: Amazon FSx File Gateway is on the AWS maintenance list since 2024-10-28; teach it as old-question knowledge.

claim: AWS OpsHub is an application you download from the Snowball resources page that gives a graphical user interface for managing Snowball devices.
question: What is AWS OpsHub for AWS Snowball?

values.display: graphical user interface for managing the AWS Snowball devices

evidence.quote: AWS OpsHub is an application that you can download from the Snowball resources page. It offers a graphical user interface for managing the AWS Snowball devices.
